title: Mass Number and Isotopes
topicTitle: Discovery Of Neutron And Fundamental Particles
notes: Mass number A, the isotope concept it makes possible, and the average-atomic-mass calculation — the accounting that sits on top of the fundamental particles.

A = number of protons + number of neutrons = Z + N. It is always a whole number because it counts particles; the *atomic mass* measured for an element is usually not a whole number because it is a weighted average over isotopes (e.g. Cl = 35.45 u). Notation ᴬZX places A upper-left, Z lower-left.
• Hydrogen: ¹H protium, ²H deuterium (D, in heavy water D₂O), ³H tritium (radioactive) — the only element whose isotopes have separate names.
• Carbon: ¹²C (98.9%, the amu standard), ¹³C (NMR), ¹⁴C (dating). Chlorine: ³⁵Cl (75%), ³⁷Cl (25%). Uranium: ²³⁵U (fissile, 0.7%), ²³⁸U (99.3%).
• Chemical properties are almost identical (same electron configuration); physical properties differ with mass (density, diffusion rate, spectra — the D line shift identified deuterium).

Average = Σ(abundance × isotopic mass). Cl: 0.75 × 35 + 0.25 × 37 = 35.5 u. Ne: 0.905 × 20 + 0.0027 × 21 + 0.0923 × 22 ≈ 20.18 u. Working backwards: given the average and one abundance, the second isotopic mass can be found.

Because isotopes differ only in mass, separation uses mass-dependent processes: gaseous diffusion (UF₆) or centrifugation for ²³⁵U, electrolysis/distillation for D₂O. Uses: ¹⁴C dating, ¹³¹I thyroid therapy, ⁶⁰Co radiotherapy, D₂O as a neutron moderator, tracer studies in metabolism.
Isotopes violate Dalton's postulate that all atoms of an element are identical in mass; the nuclear model plus the neutron explains them — same proton count, different neutron count.
confusion: ❌ Mass number is the atomic mass. ✅ A is a whole-number particle count; atomic mass is the weighted average in u.
❌ Isotopes have different chemical properties. ✅ Nearly identical chemically; they differ in mass and nuclear stability.
❌ ²³⁵U and ²³⁸U are isobars. ✅ They are isotopes (same Z = 92); isobars need equal A.

Heavy water (D₂O) is used as moderator-cum-coolant in CANDU reactors.

examples: **Problem:** An element of average mass 10.8 consists of isotopes 10 and 11. Find abundances. **Solution:** let x be the 10-isotope fraction: 10x + 11(1 − x) = 10.8 → x = 0.2 → 20% mass-10 (boron).

summary: The mass number A counts particles: A = protons + neutrons = Z + N, always a whole number, written as a left superscript in ᴬZX. It must not be confused with the atomic mass, which is a weighted average over isotopes and is usually not a whole number (Cl = 35.45 u). Isotopes are atoms of one element with the same Z and different A, so they share nearly identical chemical properties — the electrons decide chemistry — while differing in mass and nuclear stability. Hydrogen's ¹H, ²H (deuterium, in heavy water) and ³H (tritium, radioactive) are the only isotopes with separate names; carbon has ¹²C (98.9%, the amu standard), ¹³C (NMR) and ¹⁴C (dating); chlorine ³⁵Cl (75%) and ³⁷Cl (25%), giving 35.5 u by 0.75 × 35 + 0.25 × 37; uranium ²³⁵U (0.7%, fissile) and ²³⁸U. Because they differ only in mass, isotopes are separated by diffusion or centrifugation and used in dating, tracer and radiotherapy work.
importantConcepts: Mass number A = Z + N, a whole-number particle count written as a left superscript in ᴬZX
Atomic mass is a weighted average over isotopes: average = Σ(abundance × isotopic mass)
Isotopes share Z and differ in A, so chemistry is nearly identical while mass and nuclear stability differ
Separation by mass-dependent processes (UF₆ diffusion, centrifugation) and uses in dating, tracers and radiotherapy
importantStatements: Mass number is a whole-number count of particles; atomic mass is an average in u and is usually not a whole number.
Isotopes have almost identical chemical properties but different physical properties and different nuclear stability.
¹²C defines the unified mass unit: 1 u = 1/12 of a ¹²C atom = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
Chlorine's 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl give 0.75 × 35 + 0.25 × 37 = 35.5 u.
Isotopes contradict Dalton's postulate that all atoms of an element are identical in mass and properties.

keyPoints: A = Z + N; neutrons = A − Z.
Neon's average comes from three isotopes: 0.905 × 20 + 0.0027 × 21 + 0.0923 × 22 ≈ 20.18 u.
Boron works out at 0.20 × 10 + 0.80 × 11 = 10.8 u, matching the tabulated 10.81 u.
Heavy water (D₂O) is a moderator-cum-coolant in CANDU reactors; reactor fuel needs ≈3–5% ²³⁵U.
specialNotes: Isotopes are separated only by mass-dependent methods because their chemistry is identical.
²³⁵U and ²³⁸U are isotopes (same Z = 92), not isobars — isobars need equal A.
The ¹⁴C/¹²C ratio with its 5730-year half-life is the basis of carbon dating.

Weighted averages are set up as: average = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂ + …) with fractions summing to 1.
